archetypes.name: shell-portability
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces new shell patterns in both SKILL.md and write-session-env.sh; verify all proposed constructs comply with the Bash 3.2 and BASH_AUTHORING.md constraints that govern this repo.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check every new or modified shell construct the plan proposes against the repo's Bash 3.2 portability rules (BASH_AUTHORING.md). Verify the new SKILL.md one-liner uses POSIX `[` brackets rather than `[[`, that `. "$IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR/plugin-root.env"` (not `source`) is used, and that `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}` / `${IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR:-}` parameter forms are safe under `set -u`. Check the write-session-env.sh additions for any `[[...]]` guards, `declare -A`, or other Bash 4+ constructs that would break on macOS system Bash 3.2. Flag any `mktemp` invocation shape or `&>>` redirection that deviates from the portable alternatives required by BASH_AUTHORING.md. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: site-count-accuracy
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims exactly 40 executable replacement sites (37 post-Step-0 + 3 pre-bootstrap) but the description text cites both ~41 and 43; a count mismatch leaves live awk fences in SKILL.md after the PR merges.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify the plan's fence-site counts against evidence in skills/implement/SKILL.md: the description prose says the 'Bash block prelude' section itself claims 43 sites, but the plan targets 40 executable (37 post-Step-0 source-only + 3 pre-bootstrap source+awk) plus one prose-example non-executable site. Determine whether the discrepancy (40 vs 41 vs 43) is explained by which sites are executable vs prose, or whether the plan's count is wrong and additional sites would be missed. Check whether the pre-bootstrap sites at the specific plan-named locations (:105-108, :307-311, :466-469) are accurately identified as the only three that need the source+awk two-liner, and that no other early-bootstrap sites exist. Confirm the plan's instruction to 'match on the byte-identical 4-line block, not absolute offsets' is robust given that line numbers shift as edits are applied and that the plan still lists absolute line numbers that implementers may rely on. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: writer-source-safety
archetypes.rationale: The plan refactors write-session-env.sh to be source-safe via a BASH_SOURCE guard so implement-bootstrap.sh can dot-source it to load emit_plugin_root_env; any global side-effects or missing guards in the refactored file would corrupt the bootstrap environment.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit whether the planned BASH_SOURCE guard refactor of scripts/write-session-env.sh is safe to source from implement-bootstrap.sh. Check if write-session-env.sh currently has top-of-file global side-effects (set -euo pipefail, global variable initialization, trap setup, or unconditional output) that would fire when the file is dot-sourced, even after the main body is wrapped in a BASH_SOURCE guard. Verify that the proposed emit_plugin_root_env function, defined before argument parsing, does not rely on any variables that the argument-parsing block sets (such as $OUTPUT, $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT_VALUE, or internal config vars) in ways not visible to a caller that provides only the two positional arguments. Check that the plan's implement-bootstrap.sh resume-tail call sequence — read key via read-session-env-key.sh, then source write-session-env.sh, then call emit_plugin_root_env — handles the case where LARCH_CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is an empty string or missing from session-env.sh without writing a zero-byte or malformed plugin-root.env. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
